critical_issues: Perpetual confidentiality obligation with no expiration date
24-month non-compete in entire enterprise software industry (overly broad)
24-month non-solicitation of clients Contractor 'interacted with' (could be hundreds)
Auto-renewal for 12-month terms with 60-day notice requirement
Asymmetric termination: Company 30 days, Contractor 60 days
Contractor forfeits final month compensation ($8,500) if Contractor terminates
Unlimited indemnification with no monetary cap
20 hours unpaid transition work required upon termination
Company has unilateral approval rights over all work
Non-compete scope determined by 'Company in its sole discretion'

liability_analysis.contractor_liability: Unlimited - no cap on indemnification obligations
liability_analysis.assessment: Extremely one-sided; Contractor exposed to unlimited liability while Company's liability is minimal

specific_restrictions: Cannot provide marketing services to any competitor
Cannot work for companies in enterprise software
non_compete_analysis.competitor_definition: Project management, team collaboration, or workflow automation software (as determined solely by Company)
enforceability_concerns: Extremely broad industry restriction (all enterprise software)
24 months is long for contractor relationship
May be unenforceable in some jurisdictions
'Sole discretion' clause gives Company unlimited power to define competitors
Effectively prohibits Contractor from working in their field for 2 years
non_compete_analysis.financial_impact: Could eliminate 50-80% of potential clients for 2 years

non_solicitation_analysis.employee_restriction: Cannot solicit, recruit, or hire any Company employees/contractors
non_solicitation_analysis.client_restriction: Cannot solicit clients or prospects Contractor 'interacted with'
scope_concerns: Could include hundreds of clients if managing Company's accounts
Viewing a client's LinkedIn profile might constitute 'interaction'
24 months is long for preventing client contact
May prevent Contractor from working with existing clients from before engagement

confidentiality_concerns: Perpetual confidentiality with no time limit or expiration
Covers business strategies, customer lists, pricing, financials, product roadmaps, marketing plans
Breach can result in 'immediate termination and legal action'
Very broad definition of confidential information
No carve-outs for information that becomes public or was independently known
termination_risks: Auto-renewal for 12-month terms unless 60 days notice given
Easy to miss renewal deadline and be locked in another year
Company can terminate with 30 days notice
If Contractor terminates, forfeits entire final month ($8,500)
Must provide 20 hours unpaid transition work
10-day cure period for breach is short
ip_and_work_product: All work is 'work for hire' belonging to Company
Includes all content, strategies, campaigns, reports, creative work
Contractor cannot reuse or reference work in portfolio without permission
Company owns all social media followers, engagement, account assets
Contractor must transfer all admin rights and cannot export data
Reasonable for work-for-hire arrangement but eliminates portfolio building
compensation_concerns: $8,500/month for 30-35 hours/week = $49-$57/hour (below market for experienced marketer)
20 social posts/week + 4 blogs/month + 8 email campaigns = substantial workload
Forfeit final month if Contractor terminates ($8,500 penalty)
Annual value $102,000 but net of insurance is $98,000-100,000

workload_analysis.assessment: Workload likely exceeds 30-35 hours, especially during campaign launches

approval_requirements: Company must approve all content before publication
Company can reject work and require unlimited revisions at no cost
Approval required for new campaigns, ad creative, blog posts, strategy changes, expenditures over $500
Creates significant bottleneck and potential for scope creep via endless revisions

insurance_requirements.availability: May be difficult to obtain for marketing contractors

social_media_control: Company retains ownership of all accounts and assets
Can revoke Contractor access at any time
Contractor cannot claim followers or engagement
Cannot export data for personal use
Must transfer all admin rights upon termination
Reasonable from Company perspective but limits Contractor's portfolio and case studies
performance_evaluation: Evaluated on engagement rates, traffic, leads, email performance, ROAS
Company can reject work that doesn't meet quality standards
Subjective quality assessment could lead to disputes
Marketing results depend on many factors outside Contractor's control
regulatory_compliance_risks: Contractor warrants compliance with FTC guidelines and platform policies
Must comply with GDPR, CCPA, CAN-SPAM
Advertising regulations complex and constantly changing
Contractor liable for violations even if Company approved the content
dispute_resolution: Company can seek injunctive relief in court for confidentiality/non-compete breaches
Reasonable process but location may be inconvenient for remote Contractor
rationale: This contract has several dangerous provisions that create excessive risk for the Contractor. The unlimited indemnification, 24-month non-compete covering the entire enterprise software industry, perpetual confidentiality, auto-renewal, asymmetric termination rights, and forfeiture of final month's pay are all problematic. The $8,500/month compensation may be insufficient given the workload, responsibilities (managing $240K-300K annual ad budget), and insurance requirements. The non-compete's 'sole discretion' clause gives Company unlimited power to define competitors. However, the work-for-hire IP arrangement is standard for this type of engagement.
required_changes_to_accept: Cap indemnification at $50,000 or 6 months compensation
Narrow non-compete to specific competing products (not entire industry)
Remove 'sole discretion' language from competitor definition
Limit non-solicitation of clients to those Contractor directly managed accounts for
Change confidentiality from perpetual to 2-3 years
Make termination notice symmetric (both parties 30 days or both 45 days)
Remove forfeiture of final month's compensation
Reduce unpaid transition work to 10 hours maximum
Remove auto-renewal or reduce notice period to 30 days
Limit revision requests to 2 rounds per deliverable
Increase compensation to $10,000-11,000/month given workload and ad budget responsibility
Add mutual liability cap or increase Company's liability cap
deal_breakers: If unlimited indemnification cannot be capped
If non-compete cannot be reduced below 18 months or narrowed in scope
If perpetual confidentiality cannot be limited to reasonable term
If forfeiture of final month's pay cannot be removed
If compensation cannot be increased to reflect actual workload
strengths_of_contract: Clear scope of work and deliverables defined
Work-for-hire IP arrangement is standard for contractor marketing work
Company appropriately owns social media accounts and assets
Reasonable that Company has approval rights over public-facing content
Each party bears own arbitration costs (not one-sided)
Quarterly performance reviews provide feedback opportunity
